title: Partial response sweep policy and graceful resume protocol
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Reduce customer-visible failures and resource leakage caused by interrupted streaming generations (client disconnects, client-side timeouts, and network flaps) while enabling robust resume behavior for long-running outputs. This ticket defines a sweep/cleanup policy for orphaned generation fragments and a graceful resume protocol that interoperates with existing KV prefix caching and checkpoint markers. We want to avoid both: (a) prematurely dropping fragments that a client can still resume, and (b) letting stale fragments consume GPU/metadata resources for long periods.
acceptance_criteria: New sweep daemon removes orphaned generation fragments after configurable grace windows and logs reconciliations to the console metrics pipeline.
Resume handshake implemented: client can present a resume token + last-known-sequence to reclaim an interrupted generation if fragment(s) are present and within retention window.
Rollout gate: by default sweep retention = 10 minutes for ephemeral sessions; can be increased per-customer for Dedicated/Private deployments.
Metric targets: orphaned fragment count reduced by >=95% compared to baseline after 2 weeks of rollout; successful resume rate >=99% within retention window for sessions started after rollout.
End-to-end tests and chaos tests added to CI that simulate abrupt disconnects, reconnects with valid/invalid resume tokens, and concurrent sweep and resume races.
design_decisions: Use server-side 'checkpoint marker' objects instead of relying solely on KV cache TTLs; markers carry: session_id, generation_id, sequence_range, last_activity_ts, resume_token_hash.
Sweep daemon (sweepd) runs partitioned across shards to avoid coordinated GC spikes; it performs idempotent reconciliation and emits reconciliation events to tracing pipeline.

Resume protocol uses a two-step optimistic handshake: 1) client presents resume_token and last_seq -> server validates marker and attaches ephemeral lease, 2) client requests delta tokens starting at last_seq+1. If validation fails, server falls back to start-over variant and returns structured error with suggested model/config.
To minimize cross-tenant risk, resume tokens are opaque HMACs tied to customer_id + model_id + generation_id with rotation support; servers only match token hashes and lease TTLs.
Retention windows are configurable by deployment tier: hosted defaults to 10m, dedicated can configure 1h, private allows admin override.
We prefer eventual consistency for sweepd to avoid blocking critical request paths; immediate reclamation only on explicit session-close signals from client or control-plane.
Observability: every sweep action emits structured events (reason=idle|timeout|resource-pressure|explicit-close), counts, and latency histogram for reclamation work.
implementation_notes: Add new DB table 'checkpoint_markers' with compact schema; store SHA256 of resume_token only (never store raw tokens).
Extend existing stream controller to create marker on first response chunk and refresh last_activity_ts on each flush or client ACK.
Implement sweepd as a background worker in runtime control-plane; run per-region with leader election using existing etcd lease layer.
Lease semantics: when a resume succeeds, sweepd must observe lease transfer to avoid racing double-consumption; implement short fence token on marker to serialize resume vs sweep.
Add API surface: /v1/streams/{generation_id}/resume (POST) accepting {resume_token, last_sequence, client_metadata} and returning {status, start_sequence, advice}.
Graceful degradation: if resume not possible, return structured fallback payload with reason codes and automatically attempt model-variant fallback if configured.
Instrument metrics: sweep_attempts_total, sweep_reclaimed_fragments_total, resume_attempts_total, resume_success_total, resume_latency_ms_p50/p95.
Add migration script for existing ephemeral artifacts to backfill checkpoint_markers from current KV prefix metadata with conservative timestamps.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): Deploy sweepd and resume API to Canary region with retention=30m for low-traffic customers. Monitor metrics and error budgets for 72h.
Phase 2 (Staged): Enable default retention=10m for 25% of traffic under feature-flag; run synthetic reconnect tests and chaos-runbook.
Phase 3 (GA): Promote to all regions, expose retention config in Console for Dedicated/Private customers, publish runbook for support.
Emergency rollback: feature-flag to turn off sweepd and a kill-switch to treat markers as infinite TTL until rollback completes.
metrics: orphaned_fragments_gauge: count of active fragments without an attached client session
reclaimed_fragments_total: total fragments cleaned by sweepd
average_resume_latency_ms: p50/p95 targets (p95 < 75ms for token validation path)
secondary: memory/GPU reclaim rate after sweep actions, to demonstrate resource salvage.
test_plan: Unit tests for marker creation, lease transfer, and token hash validation.
End-to-end integration tests simulating: client disconnect after partial flush, resume within retention, resume after retention expired.
Chaos tests: introduce race where sweepd starts reclaim concurrently with resume; assert idempotent outcome and no double-deliveries.
Load test to validate sweepd shard scaling: ensure reclaim work does not add >5% CPU overhead to control plane under typical traffic.
Manual QA checklist: verify console shows reclamation events, check audit logs for Dedicated/Private customers.
